prompt: Match each line from the thread to the kind of conflict it is.

pairs.left: "Who decides quotas, and can they change after an RFC?"
"Checkout breaks everything and blames everybody else"

prompt: What practical reading does the lesson take from the later research on task conflict?

choices.text: Settle it quickly, on its merits, before it turns personal
choices.why: Right: task conflict also hurts, especially once it feels personal.

choices.text: Let the tech lead with more seniority decide every task conflict
choices.why: Seniority is not a merit-based resolution.

choices.text: Encourage task conflict, since it shows people care about the work
choices.why: That was the earlier view, which later work complicated.

choices.text: Avoid technical debate in teams altogether
choices.why: Disagreement still has to be resolved; the point is how fast.

prompt: Match each Thomas–Kilmann mode to its short description.
Why did Lívia move the quota argument out of the platform channel?

choices.text: Because channels are for announcements only and not discussion
choices.why: No such rule; the point is about face.

choices.text: In public, nobody changes position without losing face
choices.why: Right: everybody performs for the audience.

choices.text: Because she wanted to decide it herself
choices.why: She was careful not to decide it.

choices.text: To hide the conflict from the other teams
choices.why: She promised to post the outcome there.

prompt: What question turned the two positions into interests?

choices.text: "Can you both accept 30 as a compromise?"
choices.why: Splitting the difference before the interests are known.

choices.text: "Who is right?"
choices.why: That keeps the positions.

choices.text: "Why did you write that line about blame in the channel?"
choices.why: That is the relationship conflict, handled later and in private.

choices.text: "What happens if you don't get that number?"
choices.why: Right: the answers revealed checkout's peak and logistics' batch.

prompt: Under the scheduled quota, how many connections does logistics get between 02:00 and 06:00?
And how many does it get the rest of the day, including the checkout peak?
Put Fisher and Ury's four principles in the order the lesson lists them.
items: Separate the people from the problem

prompt: How did Lívia handle Paulo's line about checkout blaming everybody?
hint: A relationship conflict has a history.

choices.text: She asked him alone what was behind it
choices.why: Right: logistics had been blamed in a first draft of the 6 March notes.

choices.text: She reported it to Henrique as a performance issue
choices.why: That turns a history into a file, and evaluation is not her role.

choices.text: She asked him to apologise in the channel
choices.why: A public apology would have reopened it.

choices.text: She ignored it, since the quota was settled
choices.why: The relationship conflict does not disappear with the task one.

prompt: Where did the real disagreement between Paulo and Bruna surface?

choices.text: In the cost line, since a broker would cost more than R$ 3,000 a month
choices.why: Cost was agreed; it was not the hidden disagreement.

choices.text: In writing the weights
choices.why: Right: future consumers against operability, never said aloud before.

choices.text: In the decision record afterwards
choices.why: The record captured an agreement.

choices.text: In the scoring of the two designs against the table
choices.why: The scoring came after; the disagreement was already visible.

prompt: The decision matrix comes out against the option everybody believes in. What does the lesson suggest?
hint: A tool for making disagreement visible.

choices.text: Follow the matrix; that is why it was built
choices.why: It is not a machine that produces answers.

choices.text: Add criteria until the favourite wins
choices.why: That turns the matrix into a justification.

choices.text: Drop the matrix and vote
choices.why: Votes are not how decisions are made in this course.

choices.text: Talk about which weight is wrong
choices.why: Right: the weights are probably wrong, and which one is the useful conversation.

prompt: Bruna's design had checkout write events to a table in its own database, known as an ___.
hint: Where letters wait to be sent.

prompt: Why does the decision record keep Paulo's broker "with the reason it lost at these weights"?
hint: What happens when the weights change?

choices.text: So the broker can be built later without another review
choices.why: A changed weight reopens the decision; it does not skip review.

choices.text: Because company policy requires the losing option in every record
choices.why: No policy is mentioned.

choices.text: He then has a document to point at, not a grievance
choices.why: Right: the record says what would make it worth revisiting.

choices.text: To show reviewers that alternatives were considered
choices.why: True of any record; the lesson's point is about Paulo.

prompt: Two teams keep fighting, with different people each time. Where does the lesson say to look?

choices.text: At how often the two teams meet each week
choices.why: Meeting more does not fix a boundary.

choices.text: At the incident history of the team that complains more
choices.why: Complaint volume is not a cause.

choices.text: At the team members with the strongest opinions
choices.why: Different people, same fight: it is not the people.

choices.text: At something they share that nobody owns
choices.why: Right: a table, a service, a release window.

prompt: Which of these are contracts in the lesson's sense? Choose all that apply.
hint: What the owner promises, in writing.

choices.text: A promise in a chat thread to "be careful with the table"
choices.why: Not written as a contract, and nothing to check a change against.

choices.text: The sixty-message thread
choices.why: That is the conflict, not a contract.

choices.text: The outbox event format, with a version number
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: The quota table
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: Both leads would have accepted Lívia deciding the quotas. Why did she not?

choices.text: A mediator who decides becomes the next owner
choices.why: Right: and every future argument lands on her desk.

choices.text: She did not know enough about the traffic
choices.why: She knew enough to mediate; that is not the reason.

choices.text: The RFC process forbids staff engineers from deciding quotas
choices.why: No such rule.

choices.text: So that she could blame them if it failed later
choices.why: Not the reason, and not this course's spirit.

prompt: Diego disagrees with Paulo about a test and goes straight to the head of engineering. What does the lesson call it?

choices.text: Mediation, done by somebody more senior than Lívia
choices.why: Nobody mediated; one side went over the other's head.

choices.text: A legitimate escalation, since the head owns both
choices.why: Escalation comes after the step below has been tried.

choices.text: A complaint, not an escalation
choices.why: Right: and it damages the relationship more than the disagreement did.

choices.text: Disagree and commit
choices.why: Nothing was committed to.

prompt: Why does the lesson call the agreed facts the most important part of the joint page?
hint: What does the person deciding hear?

choices.text: They are the shortest section, so they get read
choices.why: Length is not the reason.

choices.text: The head of engineering only reads facts and ignores views
choices.why: Both views are there to be read.

choices.text: They separate what is disputed from what is not, so the decider hears one account
choices.why: Right: decided in ten minutes.

choices.text: They prove which side is right
choices.why: They are what both sides accept, not a verdict.

prompt: Data and checkout disagree over whether the data team may read checkout's tables directly. Following this lesson, what comes first?

choices.text: Escalate to the head of engineering with both positions
choices.why: The first steps have not been tried.

choices.text: Let the thread run until one side gives up
choices.why: Competing by stamina decides nothing on the merits.

choices.text: Split the difference: read access on weekdays only
choices.why: A compromise before anyone knows the interests.

choices.text: Ask each side what happens if it doesn't get its way
choices.why: Right: interests before positions, then owner and contract.
